$comment: Declaration-name, call, type-position, and contextual-keyword rules. Every rule here is anchored by a lookbehind on an already-consumed reserved word or by the start of a line, so contextual keywords stay ordinary identifiers everywhere else. Reserved words themselves are never scoped here: they carry the scope the tokenizer-derived keyword rules give them.

contextual-keywords.$comment: The annotation-declaration entry is a begin/end block, not a single-line match: an annotation's parameter list opens multiline mode (GRAMMAR.md 2.1), so the closing ')' and 'targets' keyword may be several physical lines below 'annotation NAME'. The block ends by consuming the real 'targets' separator, which is always immediately preceded (ignoring a run of spaces/tabs) by the closing ')' of a parameter list or by the declaration's own name -- never by punctuation such as '(' or '=' -- so the leading lookbehind and the '(?!\s*:)' guard together keep a same-named parameter or default value (e.g. 'targets: int' or '= targets') from ending the block early. The alternate end branch is a zero-width lookahead bailout that closes the block (without consuming the triggering keyword, so it still gets its normal scope) if another root declaration keyword starts a line first, so a 'targets'-less declaration (mid-edit or malformed) cannot swallow the rest of the file.

dictionary-entry-separator.$comment: Consumes a dictionary entry's separator ('key: value' or Lua-style 'key = value') together with an immediately following type-shaped token, so the generic type-positions rule never sees that token: the lookbehind requires the separator to be directly preceded (on the same physical line, allowing only indentation-width whitespace) by a dictionary key shape -- a quoted string, a numeric literal, or a bare identifier with an optional simple call/argument list -- anchored to the start of a dictionary entry (the start of a line inside the dictionary, or right after '{' or ','). A colon that instead follows a parameter name inside a nested call or lambda signature is shielded from this anchor by #dictionary-value-parentheses, so it is left for #type-positions to scope normally.
dictionary-entry-separator.name: meta.dictionary.entry-separator.foundryscript

dictionary-value-parentheses.$comment: Shields a parenthesized region inside a dictionary value (a lambda's parameter list, or an ordinary call) from #dictionary-entry-separator. Without this, a parameter declaration that starts its own physical line inside a multiline parameter list -- 'value: int,' on its own line -- would satisfy the dictionary-entry-separator's start-of-line anchor and be mistaken for a fresh dictionary entry, suppressing the parameter's real type scope.
dictionary-value-parentheses.name: meta.dictionary.value.parenthesized.foundryscript
